subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw core own generic side-effect claim verification for Telegram/ACP visible replies, or limit core work to concrete message-delivery evidence and stranded-final recovery while routing generic claim verification to plugins/ClawHub?
rationale: Current main has partial delivery guardrails, VISION.md keeps optional policy out of core when plugins can express it, and the prior generic claim-verification issue was closed as ClawHub scope, so automation should not pick a broad runtime policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow Core To Delivery Evidence
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer review, land or reject the focused delivery-receipt and stranded-final work, and leave generic file/API success-claim verification to plugin or hook work unless a core API gap appears.

options.title: Define Generic Core Verification
options.body: Create a maintainer-approved core ledger policy for visible success claims, then implement it with live Telegram/ACP proof and compatibility tests.

options.title: Document Current Boundary
options.body: Document that OpenClaw transports final model text and does not verify arbitrary claimed side effects, then close this issue after pointing users to plugin-based verification.

recommendation.title: Narrow Core To Delivery Evidence
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer review, land or reject the focused delivery-receipt and stranded-final work, and leave generic file/API success-claim verification to plugin or hook work unless a core API gap appears.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the closest source-reply policy guardrail and authored recent adjacent auto-reply hardening, so they are the best available owner for the core-vs-plugin policy choice.
